notes: reading: A filer with a 401(k) deferral (traditional or Roth) is an active participant in an employer plan for the IRA deduction limit (26 U.S.C. 219(g)(5)); a filer with none is not, since no other plan coverage is stated.

reading: head (age 28) takes 8,000.00 of taxable IRA, SEP, 401(k) or 403(b) distributions. The additional tax on early distributions (26 U.S.C. 72(t)(1)) is 10% of a filer's taxable IRA, SEP, 401(k) and 403(b) distributions (qualified plans by their names, 4974(c)) when the filer is 59 or younger (a stated age of 59 does not state 59 1/2), less the medical exception (72(t)(2)(B): distributions up to medical expenses above 7.5% of AGI), and none for a filer disabled under 72(m)(7) (the is_disabled reading: stated disabled with no earnings of their own). Every other exception (separation from service after 55, equal periodic payments, first home, education, birth or adoption, and so on) needs an unstated fact, so none applies. A private pension is not taxed: whether the plan is a qualified plan (4974(c)) or an annuity contract (72(q)) is not stated. Tax-Calculator takes the tax as e09900; TAXSIM has no input for it. policyengine-us takes it as an input with no formula (qualified_retirement_penalty), so the key holds none; its line income_tax_before_refundable_credits adds it when stated.
itemized_notes: reading: Stated other health insurance premiums are not counted again: policyengine-us documents them as part of the stated premiums without Medicare Part B (variables/household/expense/health/other_health_insurance_premiums.py), so counting both would double count. Medical expenses take the premiums without Medicare Part B.
reading: Over-the-counter health expenses are left out of medical expenses: the stated amount is not said to be prescribed medicine or insulin (26 U.S.C. 213(b)) or other medical care (213(d)(1)).

board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: The household fact 'is disabled' is read as satisfying SSI's disability criterion (the engine input meets_ssi_disability_criteria, which the certified microdata never sets and the prompt never lists). Recomputed with policyengine-us 1.755.4 with each person in a correctly built marital unit; the run's own situation placed every household member in one marital unit, which deems the whole household's income to the adult and masks the change.
board_exclusion_records.judge_verdict: llm_error where any row was judged
board_exclusion_records.note: SSI itself stays $0 under either reading (the head's countable income exceeds the federal benefit rate); SNAP moves because SSI-disabled status switches on the elderly-or-disabled SNAP rules. The 2026-09-05 record gave 3,596.04 under that reading on the frozen engine; the 2026-09-22 audit recomputes it with every publication convention and upstream fix.

board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: The household fact 'is disabled' is read as not meeting the Social Security definition of disability (the engine input meets_ssi_disability_criteria, which the prompt does not list). The head's MAGI is 141.2% of the federal poverty guideline, above the 138% limit for the adult expansion group, so only a disability pathway leads to Medi-Cal. California's 250% Working Disabled Program requires the Social Security definition (42 CFR 435.540(a)); policyengine-us 2.15.17 tests the broad is_disabled flag instead and places the head in that program (medicaid_category WORKING_DISABLED_BUY_IN).
board_exclusion_records.note: Flagged in the 2026-09-29 engine upgrade by the investigation of cluster excl_snap_ssi_disability and its independent review, and excluded on review of the release (reference_audit/2026-09-28/final_actions.json, audit_exclusions). Alternative computed on 2.15.17 with the publication conventions and the Working Disabled Program's disability test reading meets_ssi_disability_criteria (reference_audit/2026-09-28/scripts/probe_023_medicaid.py); unmodified, 2.15.17 gives 1 under either reading. The same unlisted input excludes this household's SNAP.
